title: The Theory of Investment Value
question: What is a stock intrinsically worth?
changed: The present value of all future dividends: discounted cash flow as the definition of value.
assumed: Future dividends and the discount rate can be forecast.

title: The Cost of Capital, Corporation Finance and the Theory of Investment
question: Does how a firm is financed change what it is worth?
changed: In frictionless markets, no: capital structure is irrelevant and leverage only reshuffles risk between claimants.
assumed: No taxes, no bankruptcy costs, no information asymmetry.

verified.note: Crossref has no DOI for American Economic Review articles of this period.

title: Dividends, Earnings, and Stock Prices
venue: The Review of Economics and Statistics
question: What does the dividend discount model look like when dividends grow steadily?
changed: The Gordon growth model: price = next dividend / (r − g), and the terminal value in every DCF since.

title: Dividend Policy, Growth, and the Valuation of Shares
question: Does paying dividends raise firm value?
changed: Dividend policy is irrelevant given investment policy; all valuation formulas, from dividends, earnings or cash flows, agree.

title: Theory of the firm: Managerial behavior, agency costs and ownership structure
question: Who runs the firm in whose interest, and what does it cost?
changed: Agency costs of equity and debt explain ownership and capital structure where Modigliani–Miller is silent.

title: Determinants of corporate borrowing
question: Why don't firms with growth options borrow more?
changed: Debt overhang: risky debt makes shareholders pass up good investments, so growth firms borrow less.

title: Corporate financing and investment decisions when firms have information that investors do not have
question: Why does announcing a stock issue lower the price?
changed: Managers issue equity when it is overvalued, so investors discount issuers: the pecking order of financing.

title: Earnings, Book Values, and Dividends in Equity Valuation
question: Can value be written in accounting numbers instead of dividends?
changed: Residual income valuation: value equals book value plus discounted abnormal earnings.

title: Do Stock Prices Fully Reflect Information in Accruals and Cash Flows about Future Earnings?
question: Do investors notice that accrual earnings persist less than cash earnings?
changed: They don't: high-accrual firms underperform, the accrual anomaly.

title: Value Investing: The Use of Historical Financial Statement Information to Separate Winners from Losers
question: Within cheap stocks, can simple accounting signals pick the winners?
changed: The F-score: nine binary signals of profitability, leverage and efficiency raise value returns substantially.
